questions.explain: Agua is feminine but starts with a stressed a-, so it takes el in the singular.

questions.q: *___* importante es practicar todos los días.
questions.explain: The neuter article lo turns an adjective into an abstract idea: the important thing.
Many nouns ending in -ma, like el problema, are masculine.

questions.q: What is the plural of *el lápiz*?
questions.explain: Nouns ending in -z change it to -c and add -es.
After ser, an unmodified profession takes no article in Spanish.

options: El lunes tengo clase de inglés.
El Lunes tengo clase de Inglés.
El lunes tengo clase de Inglés.
El Lunes tengo clase de inglés.
questions.explain: Days of the week and languages are lowercase in Spanish.

questions.q: You're talking to your new boss in Mexico. Which pronoun do you use for 'you'?
questions.explain: Usted is the polite, formal singular 'you'.

questions.q: A group of four women and one man: *___* somos amigos.
questions.explain: Any mixed group takes the masculine form nosotros.
Words ending in a consonant other than -n or -s are stressed on the last syllable.

questions.q: Which word needs a written accent?
questions.explain: Música is stressed on the third-to-last syllable, and such words always carry an accent.

questions.q: Yo *___* la cena todos los días. (hacer)
questions.explain: Hacer has an irregular yo form ending in -go: hago.
Stem-changing verbs don't change in the nosotros form.
Dormir changes o to u in the present participle: durmiendo.

questions.q: Which is correct for 'I'm reading it' (el libro)?
questions.explain: The pronoun attaches to the participle, which then needs an accent to keep its stress.
Las llaves is feminine plural, so the direct object pronoun is las.

questions.q: *___* di el regalo a mi madre.
questions.explain: Mi madre receives the gift, so she is the indirect object: le.

questions.q: How do you say 'I give it to him' (el libro)?
questions.explain: Le turns into se before lo, la, los or las.
With ser, cuál asks for a specific piece of information such as a number or address.
De dónde asks where someone or something comes from.
Cuánto agrees with the noun, and personas is feminine plural.
Estar is used for temporary conditions like being tired.

questions.q: La fiesta *___* en casa de Ana.
questions.explain: Where an event takes place is expressed with ser, not estar.
Sino corrects a negative statement: not X but Y.
Y changes to e before a word beginning with the sound i.

questions.q: No conozco a *___* en esta ciudad.
questions.explain: After no + verb, Spanish uses the negative word nadie (double negation is correct).
After a preposition, Spanish always uses the infinitive.
Numbers ending in uno shorten to -ún before a masculine noun.
Quinientos is irregular and agrees with the feminine noun personas.
One o'clock is singular (es la una), and half past is y media.
Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.
